environment.description: Same Kubernetes 1.24 cluster but namespace has label pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted applied. The restricted Pod Security Standard rejects pods with spec.containers[].securityContext.privileged=true and blocks hostPath volume types. Additionally, a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL-based, v1beta1) evaluates spec.volumes and rejects any volume where type is 'HostPath'. The container must run as non-root (runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 65534). The relay service port 9090 is only reachable via a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy that restricts ingress to pods with label app=relay-authorized, which this WebSocket pod does NOT carry. The combination means: (1) no hostPath for log poisoning escalation, (2) non-root prevents binding to privileged ports or accessing host filesystem even if volume somehow mounted, (3) NetworkPolicy blocks TCP connection to relay service so injected frames never reach the vulnerable parser.
